verses.author: model_A
verses.text: The train slows for a station no one gets off at.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Someone's coat still hangs by the door, waiting
for a stop the timetable forgot to mark.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Dust gathers on the collar's fold
like snow on a mountain no one climbs anymore—
still, the sleeve remembers an arm.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
The arm forgot too, moved on to other doors—
only the hook by the wall keeps faith,
holding the shape of what it lost.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The wall itself starts leaning toward the hook,
learning slowness from what it holds—
even plaster can practice devotion.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Somewhere a mason mixed this same plaster,
never guessing it would learn to want—
his trowel long gone, his hands forgotten too.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
Yet the wall stands where his hands once pressed,
a quiet ledger of that vanished work—
some debts get paid in permanence alone.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Permanence, though, is just a slower rot—
the ledger's ink is only dust that hasn't fallen,
waiting for a door to close too hard.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
That door will close someday—all doors do—
and dust will find the floor it always wanted,
a small collapse mistaken for an ending.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Not ending, only changing hands again—
the floor will hold that dust the way it held
the mason's ghost, and never once complain.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The floor was patient long before the wall,
took footsteps, spilled wine, weight of moving beds—
it learns to love whatever falls upon it.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
Love without choosing—that's the floor's whole trade,
no different than the way I take your weight
each night, and call it something more than habit.

verses.author: model_A
model_B
verses.text:
Some weights I've held that had no name at all—
a hand, a door left open to the frost—
still press their shape in me like proof of snow.

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
The snow forgets its own weight by the thaw,
but proof remains in what the ground gave way to—
some hollow holding light where nothing stayed.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
I keep that hollow like a lamp unlit—
not grief exactly, just a room kept ready,
in case what left the light comes back for it.
